evidence.note: GPU-generated Work Graph input validation, GPU command generation, and gated downstream execution path.
D3D12 producer-to-Work-Graph GPU-header fixtures and exact rejection/readback assertions.
Integrated Work Graph input, coalescing, routing, queue-dependency, and readback evidence.

rows.remaining: A compute producer writes two single-node GPU headers and payloads; thread entrypoints are GPU-selected and dense/sparse downstream routing is exact. Trace records host_header_read=0 events. Coalescing, broadcasting, covered multi-node forms and bounded rejection rows are separate closures; capacity/lifetime, larger tables and broader launch/resource breadth remain open.

An ordinary compute producer writes a D3D12_MULTI_NODE_GPU_INPUT header and two GPU node-input descriptors. The GPU validates the table and records, compacts selected entry commands and produces exact dense/sparse routing without host descriptor/header reads. Bounded malformed, duplicate, zero-table-stride, broadcasting and zero-descriptor rows also pass; larger tables and cross-queue lifetime remain open.

The same GPU-produced headers select a coalescing entrypoint with two-record batches and a thread entrypoint without host header reads. Exact dense/sparse routing and coalescing group/bitmap counters pass. Covered multi-node headers are separate evidence; broader launch, resource-argument, table-capacity and lifetime breadth remains open.

A GPU-produced header selects a fixed 2x2x2 broadcasting entrypoint. Each command binds one record and all eight groups read it through the raw single-record context; atomic sums prove all contributions. The previous stream-context version dropped contributions for nonzero X groups. Broader grid/thread shapes, system-value semantics and resource arguments remain open.

A GPU-produced multi-input table expands one broadcasting descriptor into four GPU-native commands, each with a raw single-record context and an exact 2x2x2 grid, while a second thread descriptor contributes 505. The atomic output proves every group and descriptor ran once. Larger broadcasting tables and broader resource/system-value arguments remain open.

A GPU-produced table whose broadcast record expansion plus a second descriptor exceeds the bounded ICB capacity rejects before backing reset or command encoding; the full 2 MiB sentinel remains unchanged.
Two identical GPU-produced broadcasting descriptors execute independently and atomically double every dense contribution. Larger duplicate tables and cross-queue lifetime remain open.
A GPU-produced multi-input header with zero descriptor-table stride rejects before table dereference and preserves the full backing sentinel.
A GPU-produced child entrypoint outside the immutable table rejects without an allocator reset, output writes or ICB execution. Other malformed multi-header cases remain separate rows.

A zero-count child with an unused UINT64_MAX payload pointer is skipped while a later nonempty sparse child contributes exactly 505 through an atomic sum. Broader empty-child permutations, table sizes and queue dependencies remain open.

A compute-produced table address misaligned by one byte rejects before child descriptor dereference. All 2 MiB of backing memory and user output remain unchanged. Other address/range and lifetime combinations remain open.

Three GPU-produced zero-stride records form batches of two and one: atomic sum 303, group count two and batch-size bitmap six. An independent sparse child produces 505. Larger batches, capacities and cross-queue replication remain open.

Four zero-stride records form two coalescing batches of two. An atomic downstream sum of 404, batch count two and batch-size bitmap four prove exact replication and grouping; the independent sparse child produces 505. Partial batches and larger streams remain open.

A GPU-produced child descriptor with four records and zero record stride replicates value 101 four times; an atomic downstream sum proves exact multiplicity without overlapping non-atomic writes. The independent sparse child still produces 505. Descriptor-table zero stride, larger streams and coalescing replication remain open.

A valid first descriptor followed by an invalid entrypoint rejects the entire GPU-produced input table. All user output words and the entire 2 MiB backing allocation (including allocator metadata, payload slots and trailing bytes) remain unchanged under an offset-varying sentinel. Larger mixed tables remain open.
A GPU-produced descriptor count beyond the bounded ICB capacity rejects before backing reset and execution.
A GPU-produced descriptor stride below the child-header ABI rejects without writes or allocation.
A GPU-produced record span outside registered address bounds rejects the entire multi-input dispatch atomically.
A GPU-produced zero-descriptor input is valid no-work and preserves the allocator table.
Empty-output to payload-input mismatch rejects before either producer writes or allocates. Broader malformed layouts and creation-time compatibility validation remain open.
Runtime thread/group counts publish logical empty records to a coalescing consumer; group reservation occurs once. Empty-output arrays, recursive empty routing and broader limits remain open.
Zero thread/group requests consume no records/allocations and launch no consumers. General overflow/recycling remains open.
31 self-steps plus entry execute all 32 levels exactly once. Broader mixed-node depth accounting remains open.
A 33-level expansion rejects before writes/reset while an independent dispatch completes. No SetProgram initialization is requested. Creation-time graph-depth validation remains open.
Four input records recurse in two-record coalescing batches; exact group count and batch-size bitmap pass. Partial batches and broader launch/resource combinations remain open.
GPU publication stops before the declared leaf; later encoded levels do no work. Broader termination and boundary combinations remain open.

Record-driven broadcasting recurses through native ICB contexts with exact levels/leaf validity; queue trace records three ICB encodes. Coalescing, GPU entry headers, variable grids and broader recursive ICB combinations remain open.
Four thread-node levels and leaf IsValid pass; declaration-only nonrecursive query returns zero. Other launch modes, GPU inputs and boundary breadth remain open.
Two self-output ports preserve per-level generations and leaf validity. Broader recursive topology/resource/output-limit combinations remain open.

Four dense targets and sparse index 65536 route exactly; sparse misses and post-recording CPU mutation are covered. GPU input, routed ICB consumers, recursion, output limits and broader array shapes remain open.
Valid dense/sparse array graphs create; a missing required dense target rejects at creation. A separate bounded array-dispatch row passes; broader array shapes remain open.
Six empty CPU records batch as four and two under MaxRecords(4); broader empty launch forms and empty-output routing remain open.
CPU-authored GPU headers carry six empty records with exact batch counts; GPU-generated headers and empty-output routing remain open.
CPU-authored GPU header with a single empty record is verified; GPU-generated headers and broader empty-record launch forms remain open.
A GPU header without payload is rejected for a nonempty record layout before writes. Broader malformed-header cases remain open.
A single null-payload, zero-stride CPU record reaches EmptyNodeInput with count 1. Broader empty-record launch forms, GPU-generated headers and empty-output routing remain open.
Payload-less input to a nonempty record layout rejects before shader writes. Broader malformed input forms remain open.
Direct and native-ICB dynamic-grid paths converge with exact once-only contributions. General topology, output arrays and overflow remain open.
Conditional zero/two publication feeds compacted native-ICB dynamic consumers without inactive-route writes. General conditional topology and overflow remain open.
Gated compute-queue copy feeds entry broadcasting, native-ICB dynamic consumers and coalescing. GPU-generated entry headers and broader multi-queue graph patterns remain open.
GPU-produced U32 XYZ grids drive native per-record indirect commands and a coalescing sink. General topology, output arrays, recursion and GPU-generated input headers remain open.
GPU-produced U16 XYZ grids at metadata-defined offsets are verified; broader record layouts and overflow semantics remain open.
An empty GPU descriptor stream produces an empty ICB execution range. General cancellation/reuse semantics remain open.
Individual zero X/Y/Z grids launch no consumer work while the nonzero record route completes. General malformed-grid behavior remains open.
Two native-ICB chains in one command list preserve independent command/range/context storage and pipelines. Broader concurrent graph reuse remains open.

PE/Unix bridge executes GPU-generated native compute commands with a GPU-selected range. Bounded D3D12 dynamic consumers have separate integration probes; broader ICB lifetime/residency coverage remains open.
An empty GPU-generated ICB range skips all commands, including the poison command. This is bridge feasibility, not D3D12 dynamic-grid support.

Same-named graphs in distinct state objects retain independent shaders. Surviving identifiers remain usable after peer destruction; retired identifiers do not execute a shader or synthetic fallback. AddToStateObject inheritance and broader multigraph semantics remain open.
Two chains in one command list preserve distinct records and per-dispatch allocator state despite CPU-record mutation. General concurrent graph/backing reuse remains open.
Adjacent lanes in each two-thread broadcasting group request zero/one output records independently. General output limits, wave-width combinations and overflow remain open.
Input-driven group allocation of zero or two output records is verified. General output-count limits and overflow semantics remain open.
Input-driven thread allocation of zero or one output record is verified; unrestricted publication and sharing semantics remain open.
Zero upstream records skip fixed-grid downstream groups despite non-unit Y/Z. Broader empty and conditional-output graph patterns remain open.

Fixed 2x2x2 downstream broadcasting with two threads per group and record-local group/thread IDs is verified. Broader record-driven consumer layouts, recursion and general resource tables remain open.
An unconnected 264-byte output rejects before entry writes because bounded slots are 256 bytes. Larger-record execution remains unsupported.
Compute-queue copy into DEFAULT-heap records, gated producer and dependent direct-queue chain. GPU-generated headers and broader multi-queue graph synchronization remain open.
Same-queue copy and transition into DEFAULT-heap records; GPU-generated headers remain open.
U16 three-axis grid at byte offset 2 in an 8-byte record is verified. Additional GPU-produced U16 payload/layout combinations and overflow remain open.

Self-recursive downstream node rejects before entry shader side effects, even with NodeMaxRecursionDepth metadata. This certifies fail-closed behavior only; recursive execution and remaining-recursion semantics are still unsupported.

Mismatched producer/consumer record sizes reject without upstream shader writes or allocations. Fixed and record-driven downstream broadcasting have separate positive witnesses; runtime expansion-bound probes remain open.
Two distinct outputs converge through direct and intermediate-node paths. Output arrays, recursion and general graph topology remain open.
Exactly 256 allocations and 320 records with multiple coalescing batches. Behavior beyond allocation capacity and dynamic backing sizing remain open.
Upload-backed GPU input with CPU publication after recording is verified. Cross-queue GPU-produced chain payloads and GPU-generated input headers remain open.
Bounded U32 three-axis grids with non-unit Y and Z are verified; unrestricted graph topology and overflow semantics remain open.
Scalar U32 grid at byte offset 4 in a 16-byte record is verified; unrestricted graph topology remains open.
Mixed zero/nonzero scalar grids only; multidimensional and general record layouts remain open.
Four zero scalar grids produce no downstream records; this is not general empty graph or cancellation coverage.

Bounded broadcasting-to-thread-to-coalescing chain only, with first-field scalar record grids and groupshared reduction. General grid layouts, fan-out, recursion, output arrays, resource/argument tables and overflow semantics remain open; dirty-source staging is not release provenance.

The source-owned native Metal AS/MS provider covers the exact 256-byte payload, two dispatch groups, direct and indirect dispatch, array layers, depth bounds, blend, wireframe, resource bindings, and statistics witnesses. Broader payload/topology/resource/barrier/VRS combinations remain open.
Four source-owned SM5 geometry fixtures link through the object/mesh provider; draw/readback breadth and DXIL geometry remain open.

The proof implements one GPU-native reference node kernel, one source-owned DXIL node-library lowering path, graph properties, backing memory, three-record CPU-input dispatch, GPU-input descriptor dispatch, two-node CPU/GPU input flattening with entrypoint routing, local-root-index reporting, INCLUDE_ALL_AVAILABLE_NODES metadata materialization, explicit backing-memory initialization, bounded output-record allocation/publication, and exact readback without a CPU scheduler. Fixed-grid broadcasting/thread nodes prove two-record CPU/GPU input routing with GPU execution and post-recording CPU mutation. Coalescing nodes now prove declared-MaxRecords batching, dynamic input indexing, six-record CPU/GPU input routing, and exact readback. Recursive/fan-out graphs, downstream scheduling, multi-entrypoint resource/record routing, barriers, and general DXIL node shader conversion remain open.
